name: System Beep Driver
description: This affects the old system beep behavior driven by the Beep driver. Most people will never notice it unless they are cleaning up legacy system sounds or debugging old compatibility behavior.

name: Disable Spatial Audio
description: Sets the DisableSpatialOnLowLatency audio policy value to disable spatial audio on the low-latency path.

name: Disable System Sounds
description: Clears the default sound events for common system sounds.

name: Show Disconnected Audio Devices
description: This makes disconnected audio devices appear in the classic Sound control panel. The evidence only proves the DeviceCpl preference is read by mmsys.cpl and can be toggled reversibly.

name: Show Hidden Audio Devices
description: This makes hidden audio devices appear in the classic Sound control panel. The evidence only proves the DeviceCpl preference is read by mmsys.cpl and can be toggled reversibly.

name: Clear Wallpaper History
description: Clears the personalization wallpaper history registry entries and cached background files.

name: Cleanup Component Store
description: Cleans up the Windows component store (WinSxS folder) to free up disk space. This is a safe operation that removes superseded components and reduces the size of the component store.

name: Clear Delivery Optimization Files
description: Deletes Delivery Optimization cache used for Windows Update P2P sharing. The DoSvc service will be stopped.

name: Clear DirectX Shader Cache
description: Clears DirectX and vendor shader caches (NVIDIA, AMD, Intel). Shaders will be recompiled on next app launch.

name: Disable Reserved Storage
description: Disables Windows Reserved Storage, which reserves disk space for updates and temporary files.

name: Clear System Event Log
description: Clears the Windows System event log. WARNING: Logs cannot be recovered after clearing.

name: Clear Font Cache
description: Clears the Windows font cache. Use this if fonts are not rendering properly. The FontCache service will be stopped and restarted.

name: Clear Temporary Internet Files
description: Clears legacy WinINet cache (INetCache, INetCookies, WebCache, History). Used by Explorer, old Control Panel, and some installers.

name: Clear Memory Dump Files
description: Deletes %WINDIR%\\MEMORY.DMP and files under %WINDIR%\\Minidump.

name: Clear Prefetch Files
description: Clears Windows prefetch files from %WINDIR%\\Prefetch. Files may be regenerated by Windows over time.

name: Remove Product Key from Registry
description: Runs slmgr.vbs /cpky to remove the Windows product key from the registry. Rollback does not restore the key automatically.

name: Empty Recycle Bin
description: Empties the Recycle Bin for all drives. Files cannot be recovered after deletion.

name: Clear Shadow Copies
description: Removes all shadow copies (volume backups) to free up disk space. WARNING: This permanently removes System Restore points and volume snapshots.

name: Clear SRUM Database
description: Deletes the System Resource Usage Monitor (SRUM) database which tracks app, service, and network usage.

name: Clear Temporary Files
description: Deletes temporary files from user and system temp folders. Files in use will be skipped.

name: Clear Thumbnail Cache
description: Clears Explorer thumbnail cache files. Thumbnails will be regenerated when needed.

name: Clear Windows Error Reporting Files
description: Deletes Windows Error Reporting (WER) crash dumps and report metadata from system and user folders.

name: Delete Windows.old Folder
description: Removes previous Windows installation files from Windows.old. WARNING: You will not be able to roll back to the previous Windows version after deletion.

name: Clear Windows Update Cache
description: Resets the Windows Update cache directories (SoftwareDistribution and catroot2). Windows Update metadata will be downloaded again.

name: Docker Desktop WSL 2 Backend
description: Docker Desktop can use the WSL 2 backend on Windows. The app writes Docker's documented settings-file field and does not claim a measured performance change.

name: .NET CLI Telemetry Opt-Out
description: The .NET SDK and CLI can send telemetry about tool usage. This tweak sets the current user's opt-out environment variable so new .NET CLI sessions stop sending that telemetry.

name: Windows Long Paths
description: Windows can remove the old 260-character path limit. That helps many compatible applications, especially developer tools and projects with very deep folder trees.

name: Global Node.js Memory Limit Override
description: This tweak makes Node.js start with a larger memory limit by default. It can help very large builds or monorepos, but it also makes Node processes use more memory budget.

name: PowerShell Script Execution Policy
description: PowerShell execution policy controls which scripts are allowed to run. RemoteSigned allows local scripts and requires downloaded scripts to be signed.

name: Enable Windows Long Paths for Python Workflows
description: Some Python environments fail on Windows when project folders get very deep. Enabling Windows long paths removes the old 260-character path limit for compatible applications, including Python workflows that rely on the operating system long-path setting.

name: SSH Agent Auto-start
description: ssh-agent keeps SSH keys loaded so Git and terminal sessions can use them more easily. Auto-starting it can make developer login sessions more convenient.

name: Enable Windows Terminal Developer Features
description: Enables advanced features in Windows Terminal like debug tap and developer mode settings.

name: VS IntelliSense DisableAutoUpdating Setting
description: Writes the Visual Studio DisableAutoUpdating IntelliSense value used by this tweak.

name: VS Solution BackgroundAnalysis Setting
description: Writes the Visual Studio BackgroundAnalysis solution-loading value used by this tweak.

name: Disable VS Code Git Autofetch
description: Disables automatic Git fetching in VS Code to reduce network usage and CPU spikes.

name: Windows Developer Mode
description: Developer Mode turns on Windows support for building, sideloading, and debugging apps. Most casual users do not need it, but developers often do.

name: WSL 2 Memory Limit
description: WSL 2 can use a lot of RAM. Microsoft documents memory limits in .wslconfig, and this tweak writes that documented setting directly.

name: Always Show Icons, Never Thumbnails
description: Explorer can show file icons instead of generating thumbnails.

name: Low Disk Space Warning
description: Windows can warn you when a drive is running low on space. People sometimes turn these warnings off on lab machines or kiosk-like systems, but most users should keep them on.

name: Taskbar Chat Icon
description: Windows 11 can show a Chat icon on the taskbar. People often hide it when they do not use Chat or want a cleaner taskbar.

name: Enable Explorer Compact View
description: Explorer compact view reduces spacing between items so more files fit on screen. Some users like the denser layout, while others prefer the roomier default view.

name: Hide Empty Drives
description: Explorer can hide or show drives that do not currently have media present.

name: Launch Folder Windows in a Separate Process
description: Explorer can run folder windows in the same process or split them into separate Explorer processes.

name: Show Compressed and Encrypted Files in Color
description: File Explorer can color compressed and encrypted NTFS items so they stand out visually.

name: Show Drive Letters First
description: Explorer can show drive letters ahead of the drive name, or leave that presentation disabled.

name: Show File Extensions
description: File Explorer can hide or show file extensions like .txt, .zip, or .exe. Many advanced users prefer to always see them.

name: Show Full Path in Explorer
description: Explorer can show the full folder path instead of a shorter title. Some advanced users prefer that when they navigate deep directories.

name: Show Hidden Files and Folders
description: File Explorer can show or hide files and folders marked with the hidden attribute. Power users often enable this to inspect more of the filesystem.

name: Show Explorer Info Tips
description: File Explorer can show or suppress pop-up descriptions for folder and desktop items when you hover them.

name: Show Protected Operating System Files
description: File Explorer can hide or reveal protected operating system files. Most people should leave them hidden, but advanced troubleshooting sometimes requires seeing them.

name: Show Recent Items In Home
description: Explorer Home can show or hide recently used files.

name: Show Status Bar
description: Explorer can show or hide its status bar at the bottom of the window.

name: Display File Icons On Thumbnails
description: Explorer can show or hide file icons on top of thumbnails.

name: Taskbar Alignment
description: Windows 11 can keep the taskbar icons centered or move them to the left. Some people prefer the older left-aligned layout.

name: Disable Microsoft Edge Features
description: Disables telemetry, personalization, sync, sidebar, shopping, rewards, and various other Edge features. Also disables Windows 8/8.1 EdgeUI features.

name: Disable Microsoft Office Telemetry
description: Disables Office telemetry logging, data collection, CEIP opt-in, feedback collection, and telemetry agent tasks for all Office applications.

name: Disable OneDrive
description: Writes OneDrive policy and Explorer values that disable default-save and sync features, set PreventNetworkTrafficPreUserSignIn, and unpin OneDrive from File Explorer.

name: Disable Visual Studio Telemetry
description: Disables Visual Studio telemetry, SQM data collection, IntelliCode remote analysis, and feedback features for VS 2015-2022.

name: Configure 7-Zip Context Menu Settings
description: Sets the 7-Zip context-menu values for CascadedMenu, ElimDupExtract, MenuIcons, and WriteZoneIdExtract.

name: NCSI Active Probing Policy
description: Windows checks internet connectivity by making active test requests. Turning those tests off can change how Windows decides whether a network has internet access.

name: Automatic Administrative Shares
description: Windows automatically creates hidden administrative shares such as C$ and ADMIN$. This setting decides whether those built-in shares are created automatically.

name: IPv6 Stack Disable Override
description: IPv6 is the newer network protocol stack that Windows expects to have available. Turning it off can break some network features even if a home network mostly feels like IPv4.

name: Link-Local Multicast Name Resolution (LLMNR)
description: LLMNR lets Windows ask nearby devices for names on the local subnet when normal DNS does not help. Modern networks often disable it, but it can still help in some small or legacy local networks.

name: Set LLTD Policies to Default Behavior
description: LLTD is part of the older Windows network discovery stack. This tweak disables the explicit LLTD mapper and responder policies so Windows falls back to the documented default LLTD behavior.

name: Set mDNS Policy to Local Settings
description: mDNS is a local-network name resolution protocol used by some discovery and service-advertising workflows. This policy setting disables the explicit mDNS policy so Windows falls back to its locally configured mDNS behavior.

name: Disable NetBIOS over TCP/IP
description: Disables NetBIOS over TCP/IP on all IP-enabled adapters using the documented per-interface Windows control surface.

name: DNS Client NetBIOS Name Resolution
description: Windows can use NetBIOS-style name resolution through the DNS client policy layer. This policy lets you fully disable it, allow it, or choose more limited modes.

name: Plaintext SMB Passwords
description: This setting decides whether Windows is willing to send an unencrypted password to certain old SMB servers. Modern systems should almost never need that behavior.

name: Smart Multi-Homed Name Resolution
description: When a PC has multiple network paths, Windows can try name lookups more aggressively across them. This policy decides whether that smart multi-homed behavior stays on.

name: SMBv1 Server Protocol Support
description: SMB is the file-sharing protocol Windows uses for network shares. SMBv1 is the old version. Modern systems should avoid it, but some very old devices still need it.

name: SMBv2 and SMBv3 Server Protocol Support
description: SMBv2 and SMBv3 are the modern Windows file-sharing protocols. Turning them off forces the machine away from the normal modern SMB stack.

name: Wi-Fi Sense Suggested Hotspot Policy
description: This controls whether Windows can automatically connect to suggested open hotspots, contact-shared networks, and some paid hotspot discovery flows.

name: LLTD Responder Driver Policy
description: The LLTD Responder lets other PCs discover this device on the local network during Windows network mapping and related discovery tasks.

name: LLTD Mapper I/O Driver Policy
description: LLTD helps Windows map and discover devices on a local network. The Mapper I/O side lets the PC ask the network about its topology.

name: Flush DNS Cache
description: Clears the DNS resolver cache. This is a one-time operation and has no rollback state.

name: Configure SMB Workstation Parameters
description: Writes the SMB workstation bandwidth-throttling and cache-lifetime values used by this tweak.

name: IPv4 Preference Override
description: This keeps IPv6 available but tells Windows to prefer IPv4 when both protocols can work.

name: Require NTLM SSP Client Session Security and 128-bit Encryption
description: This setting raises the minimum session security requirements for NTLM SSP based clients. In the app's enabled state it requires both NTLMv2 session security and 128-bit encryption.

name: Reset Winsock Catalog
description: Resets the Winsock catalog to default settings. Requires a system restart to fully apply.

name: SMB: Disable Leasing
description: Disables SMB server leasing using the documented SMB server configuration surface.

name: SMB Client Large MTU
description: Large MTU lets SMB send larger requests over the network. On modern Windows networks this usually helps file-copy and share performance.

name: SMB: Enable Multichannel
description: Enables SMB Multichannel on the documented SMB client and SMB server configuration surfaces.

name: SMB over QUIC
description: SMB over QUIC lets Windows use SMB through QUIC instead of normal TCP in supported scenarios. It is a newer transport option and not a normal baseline tweak for most people.

name: SMB Server Encryption Requirement
description: SMB encryption protects file-sharing traffic so other systems on the network cannot easily read it in transit. Turning this on at the server level makes the machine stricter about how its shared data is accessed.

name: SMB Client Metadata Cache Size Bundle
description: These values control how much SMB client metadata Windows caches and how many outstanding SMB requests it allows.

name: SMB Server Reject Unencrypted Access
description: This setting makes the SMB server reject clients that try to access shares without encryption. It is stricter than simply preferring safer behavior because noncompliant clients are actively refused.

name: Require SMB Dialect 3.1.1
description: This setting forces both SMB client and SMB server components to use only SMB 3.1.1. It is a strict compatibility boundary and can quickly block older devices or software that do not support that dialect.

name: SMB Client Signing Requirement
description: SMB signing helps Windows verify that network file-sharing traffic was not altered in transit. Requiring it makes the SMB client stricter when talking to servers.

name: SMB Server Signing Requirement
description: SMB signing helps Windows verify that file-sharing traffic was not tampered with. Requiring it on the server side makes the machine stricter about inbound SMB connections.

name: SMB Cipher Suite Order
description: This setting controls which SMB encryption cipher suites are preferred and in what order. It matters mostly for advanced SMB hardening or specific compliance requirements.

name: Windows Feedback Request Frequency
description: Windows can occasionally ask for feedback. This tweak sets a user preference intended to reduce or stop those requests.

name: Lock Screen Toast Notifications
description: Windows can show some app notifications directly on the lock screen. This policy decides whether apps can raise those lock-screen toast alerts for the current user.

name: Notification Mirroring
description: Windows can mirror some notifications to other devices. This policy decides whether that cross-device mirroring is allowed for the current user.

name: Tile Notifications
description: Tile notifications are the live updates and badges some Windows tiles can show. This policy decides whether those tile updates are allowed for the current user.

name: Toast Notifications
description: Toast notifications are the pop-up alerts apps show in Windows. This policy decides whether apps can raise those pop-ups for the current user.

name: Disable Window Animations
description: Windows can animate windows when they open, close, minimize, or restore. Turning that off reduces motion and makes transitions appear more immediate.

name: Remove Menu Show Delay
description: Windows can wait a short moment before showing some menus. Setting the delay lower makes menus appear sooner after the pointer reaches them.

name: Taskbar Animations
description: This controls whether Windows animates taskbar transitions. People turn it off when they want a less animated desktop.

name: Disable Audio Ducking
description: Disables Windows automatic volume adjustment when making calls or using communication apps. Equivalent to 'Do nothing' in Sound settings.

name: AutoPlay Event Default Action
description: Windows can remember what to do when a device or media arrives. This tweak tries to change those remembered choices so common AutoPlay events take no action.

name: Disable AutoPlay
description: AutoPlay decides what Windows does when media or devices are connected. Turning it off stops Windows from automatically offering or launching actions when drives, cameras, or phones appear.

name: Disable Sticky Keys Prompt
description: Sticky Keys can show a prompt when Shift is pressed repeatedly. Some users turn that off to avoid accidental popups while gaming or typing quickly.

name: Disable Language Switch Hotkey
description: Disables the Ctrl+Shift and Alt+Shift language-switch hotkeys.

name: Set Keyboard Repeat and Cursor Blink Values
description: Sets keyboard repeat delay to 0, repeat speed to 31, and cursor blink interval to 900 ms.

name: Disable Enhanced Pointer Precision (Mouse Acceleration)
description: Disables Enhanced Pointer Precision by setting mouse speed and threshold values to their non-accelerated configuration.

name: Disable Mouse Throttling for Background Windows
description: Disables raw mouse input throttling for background windows and sets the associated throttle duration and leeway values.

name: Enable Virtualization
description: Enable Virtualization controls legacy UAC file and registry virtualization under the Policies\System branch.

name: Allow Audio To Enable Execution Required Power Requests
description: This appears to be a kernel-adjacent Control Power setting tied to whether active audio can enable execution-required power requests. It is being tracked as a research candidate, not a user-facing tweak.

name: Allow System Required Power Requests
description: This appears to be a kernel-adjacent Control Power setting tied to how the power manager treats system-required power requests. It is being tracked as a research candidate, not a user-facing tweak.

name: Class1 Initial Unpark Count
description: Class1 Initial Unpark Count is a low-level power-manager registry value under the main Power key.

name: Hiber File Size Percent
description: Hiber File Size Percent is a low-level power-manager value under the main Power key that appears to relate to hibernation file sizing behavior.

name: Lid Reliability State
description: Lid Reliability State is a low-level power-manager registry value under the main Power key.

name: MF Buffering Threshold
description: MF Buffering Threshold is a low-level power-manager registry value under the main Power key.

name: Perf Calculate Actual Utilization
description: Perf Calculate Actual Utilization is a low-level power-manager registry value under the main Power key.

name: Power Request Override Subtree
description: This is a low-level Control\Power subtree that appears to back override handling for power requests.

name: Timer Rebase Threshold On Drips Exit
description: Timer Rebase Threshold On Drips Exit is a low-level power-manager registry value under the main Power key.

name: Disable CPU Idle States (C-States)
description: Writes the idle-state-related Control\\Power registry values used by this tweak. This changes power behavior and can increase power draw.

name: Disable CPU Core Parking
description: Writes the core-parking-related Control\\Power registry values used by this tweak, including LatencyToleranceParked, LatencyToleranceSoftParked, Class1InitialUnparkCount, and MultiparkGranularity.

name: Disable Fast Startup (Hiberboot)
description: Disables Fast Startup so shutdown uses a full kernel teardown instead of reusing the hibernated kernel session on next boot.

name: Disable Hibernation
description: Runs powercfg /hibernate off. This disables hibernation and removes hiberfil.sys.

name: Network Power and Multimedia Responsiveness
description: Writes the documented DisableTaskOffload and MMCSS SystemResponsiveness values while excluding the archived opaque NetworkThrottlingIndex write.

name: Disable Power Throttling
description: Disables Windows Power Throttling so background processes are not deprioritized by that policy surface.

name: Disable Superfetch (SysMain)
description: Disables the SysMain service that preloads frequently used applications and maintains usage heuristics.

name: Disable Windows Search
description: Disables the Windows Search indexing service. This reduces indexing activity but also slows file-search freshness and query coverage.

name: Show Hibernate Option
description: Windows can show or hide Hibernate in the power menu. This policy decides whether that shortcut is visible.

name: Show Lock Option
description: Windows can show or hide the Lock action in the user tile menu. This policy decides whether that shortcut is visible.

name: Show Sleep Option
description: Windows can show or hide Sleep in the power menu. This policy decides whether that shortcut is visible.

name: Apply Processor Performance Registry Bundle
description: Writes the PerfBoostAtGuaranteed, HighPerfDurationBoot, LatencyToleranceDefault, and PerfCalculateActualUtilization values under Control\\Power.

name: Set MMCSS Games Task Profile
description: Writes the MMCSS Games task-profile values for priority, scheduling category, SFIO priority, GPU priority, and affinity.

name: Apply Grouped Power-Control Registry Bundle
description: Writes the grouped power-control registry values used by this tweak for timer coalescing, deep I/O coalescing, event processing, parked-core tolerance, and energy estimation.

name: Session Manager Watchdog Timeouts
description: These values appear to control watchdog timeout behavior around directed power transitions. They are not normal user-facing power options and are being tracked as a low-level research lane rather than a supported tweak.

name: Microsoft Accounts on This Device
description: Windows can let people add Microsoft accounts or sign in with them on the device. This security option controls whether Microsoft accounts are allowed, partly blocked, or fully blocked.

name: Deny App Access (Except Microphone)
description: Forces Windows apps to be denied access to sensitive capabilities.

name: App capability access policies
description: These policies stop Windows apps from accessing sensitive capabilities like camera, contacts, location, and background activity.

name: Windows Activity History
description: Windows can keep track of what you did on the device and can upload some of that activity so it can appear across devices. These policy values decide whether that activity feed can exist, be published, and be uploaded.

name: Disable Advertising ID
description: Windows uses an advertising ID so apps can personalize experiences across apps. Turning it off stops apps from using that ID for cross-app personalization.

name: App Diagnostic Information Access
description: Some Windows apps can request diagnostic information about other apps. This policy decides whether apps are user-controlled, always allowed, or always denied.

name: App Launch Tracking
description: Windows can track which apps you launch so Start and Search can personalize some results. People turn it off when they want less app-usage tracking.

name: App Suggestions in Start
description: Windows can suggest promoted apps and related content in places like the Start menu. People often turn this off when they want a cleaner Start experience.

name: Disable Application Compatibility Engine and SwitchBack
description: Windows includes an Application Compatibility Engine that checks a database every time an app starts and may apply compatibility fixes. SwitchBack allows apps that detect Windows Vista or later to also receive fixes designed for older OS versions. These two policies let you disable both behaviors.

name: Disable App Device Inventory Policies
description: Windows 11 24H2 added policies that track which APIs applications use, record install events, capture application footprints, and back up Win32 app data. These four policies let you turn those collection behaviors off.

name: Disable Application Compatibility
description: Turns off Windows application compatibility components, telemetry, and related tasks.

name: Application Compatibility Telemetry
description: Windows can collect anonymous telemetry about how applications use certain system components so compatibility systems can learn from it. This policy decides whether that telemetry engine runs.

name: Background App Execution
description: Windows apps can keep running in the background to sync, refresh notifications, or finish work. This policy decides whether users control that, all apps are allowed, or all apps are denied.

name: Windows Biometrics
description: Windows can use fingerprint, face, or other biometric features for sign-in and related capabilities. This device policy controls whether biometrics are allowed at all.

name: Biometric Sign-in for Domain Accounts
description: Windows can let domain users sign in with biometrics when the device and domain setup support it. This policy controls whether domain accounts are allowed to use that biometric sign-in path.

name: Biometric Sign-in
description: Windows can let users sign in with biometrics like fingerprint or face through the credential provider. This policy controls whether that sign-in path is available.

name: Camera Device Use
description: Windows can allow or block the use of camera devices on the machine. This policy decides whether cameras are usable at all.

name: Disable CEIP
description: Opts out of Customer Experience Improvement Program data collection.

name: PowerShell and .NET CLI Telemetry Opt-Out
description: PowerShell and the .NET CLI can send telemetry about tool usage. This tweak sets the current user's opt-out environment variables so new shells and CLI sessions stop sending that telemetry.

name: Cloud Consumer Account State Content
description: Some Windows experiences can use cloud-backed consumer account state content. This policy decides whether those experiences may use that content or must fall back to default content instead.

name: Windows Copilot
description: Windows Copilot is the built-in AI assistant experience in Windows. This policy decides whether that experience is available to the signed-in user.

name: Cross-Device Sharing
description: Choose whether nearby Windows experiences stay off, work only with your devices, or are available to everyone nearby.

name: Cross-Device Experiences Machine Policy
description: Windows can let devices belonging to the same user discover each other and continue some experiences across devices. This policy controls the official machine-level part of that feature.

name: Device Name in Diagnostic Data
description: Windows diagnostic data can include the computer name. This policy decides whether that name is allowed to be sent with diagnostic data.

name: Diagnostic Data Deletion
description: Windows can offer a Settings action that deletes diagnostic data associated with the device. This policy decides whether that delete option is available.

name: Diagnostic Data Viewer
description: Windows includes a viewer that can show diagnostic data categories on the device. This policy decides whether that viewer is available.

name: Edge Address Bar Suggestions
description: Microsoft Edge can show web suggestions, local history and favorites suggestions, and legacy address-bar search suggestions as you type. This bundle turns those suggestion sources off.

name: Disable F1 Help
description: Disables F1 help by renaming HelpPane.exe.

name: Microsoft Feedback Notifications
description: Windows can occasionally show prompts asking for feedback. This policy decides whether those feedback questions appear on the device.

name: File History
description: File History is Windows' built-in feature for making regular automatic backups of personal files. This policy decides whether File History can be turned on.

name: Disable Find My Device
description: Stops Windows from registering this PC with Find My Device and keeps location-based recovery turned off.

name: Online Font Providers
description: Windows can contact an online font provider to download font catalog data and, when needed, font data for rendering text. This policy decides whether that online font path is allowed.

name: Disable Inking & Typing Personalization
description: Stops sending inking and typing data to Microsoft.

name: KMS Client Online AVS Validation
description: Windows can send KMS client activation-state data to Microsoft during activation. This policy decides whether that data is sent automatically.

name: Website Access to Language List
description: Windows can let websites use your language list to show locally relevant content. This setting controls whether that language-list access is allowed.

name: Security Questions for Local Accounts
description: Windows can let local-account users create security questions so they can reset their password later. This policy decides whether those security questions are allowed.

name: Disable Location Consent (Current User)
description: This changes the current user's location permission state to deny access for packaged and desktop apps.

name: Location Consent Store (System)
description: This changes the system-level location permission state to deny access.

name: Location Scripting
description: Some scripts and apps can access Windows location features through scripting interfaces. This policy decides whether that scripting access is allowed.

name: Location Feature
description: Windows can provide location information to apps and system features. This policy decides whether the location feature is turned off for the computer.

name: MDM Enrollment
description: Windows can allow the computer to enroll into a Mobile Device Management service for remote management. This policy decides whether new MDM enrollment is allowed.

name: Message Service Cloud Sync
description: Windows can back up and restore cellular text messages through Microsoft's cloud services. This policy decides whether that cloud sync is allowed on the device.

name: Disable Offline Files
description: Disables Offline Files (CSC) via policy, services, tasks, and Sync Center.

name: Offline Files Feature Policy
description: Offline Files keeps local copies of network files so they can still be used when the computer is offline. This policy decides whether the feature is allowed at all.

name: OneSettings Downloads
description: Windows can periodically connect to the OneSettings service to download configuration settings. This policy decides whether those download attempts happen.

name: Online Tips in Settings
description: The Settings app can contact Microsoft to retrieve tips and help content. This policy decides whether those online tips are allowed.

name: Disable PCA Compatibility Diagnostics Detection
description: Windows PCA watches for compatibility issues when you run applications and drivers, and can show warnings or suggest fixes. This policy controls whether that detection runs. Disabling it stops PCA from actively monitoring for compatibility problems - it does not disable PCA itself (that is controlled separately by DisablePCA).

name: Phone-PC Linking
description: Windows can link the PC with a phone so reading, emailing, and similar tasks can continue across devices. This policy decides whether the PC can participate in that linking.

name: Disable Program Compatibility Assistant
description: Program Compatibility Assistant monitors applications and can suggest compatibility solutions when Windows detects install failures, runtime failures, or blocked drivers. This policy turns PCA off.

name: Recall Snapshot Saving
description: Recall can save snapshots of what you have seen on the screen so you can search and revisit it later. This policy decides whether those snapshots can be saved for the signed-in user.

name: Disable Resume for Current User
description: Resume lets you start on one device and continue on this PC. This tweak turns off that current-user Resume setting.

name: Resultant Set of Policy Logging
description: RSoP logging records which Group Policy settings were applied to the PC. Some people turn it off to reduce policy logging, while administrators often keep it on for troubleshooting and auditing.

name: File Explorer Search Box Suggestions
description: File Explorer can show suggestion pop-ups as you type into its search box, based on past search entries. This policy decides whether those suggestions are available.

name: Search History Storage and Display
description: Windows can remember previous search queries and use them to suggest searches later. This policy decides whether that search history is stored and shown for the current user.

name: Windows Sensors
description: Windows can use hardware sensors such as orientation, ambient light, motion, or other environmental sensors. This policy decides whether sensors are allowed.

name: Disable Sleep Study Diagnostics
description: Disables sleep study diagnostic event channels.

name: Steps Recorder
description: Steps Recorder can capture user actions and screenshots to help explain a problem. This policy decides whether the feature is available.

name: Disable Suggestions & Tips
description: Turns off Windows tips, welcome experiences, and Settings recommendations.

name: Disable Content Delivery Manager Suggestions
description: Disables various suggestions and auto-installed apps from the Content Delivery Manager.

name: Windows Suggestion Surfaces Policy Group
description: Windows uses Spotlight-like suggestion surfaces in Start, Settings, and the Windows Welcome experience. These policies control those official suggestion surfaces.

name: Disable SwitchBack Compatibility Policy
description: SwitchBack is a Windows compatibility feature that lets newer applications receive compatibility fixes originally designed for older OS versions. On a modern Windows 11 system running only current software, this feature usually has no practical effect. This policy disables it.

name: Diagnostic Data Change Notifications
description: Windows can notify the user when the diagnostic-data opt-in setting changes. This policy decides whether those notifications are shown.

name: Diagnostic Data Opt-In Settings UI
description: Windows can show controls in Settings that let a user change diagnostic data choices. This policy decides whether that Settings UI stays available.

name: Windows Error Reporting
description: Windows Error Reporting can send information about crashes and failures so Microsoft or an internal server can analyze them. This policy turns that reporting off for the device.

name: Windows Location Provider
description: Windows has a built-in location provider that apps and system features can use. This policy decides whether that provider is available.

name: Turn Off Windows Tips
description: Windows can show popups and onboarding tips that explain features and suggest ways to use the system. People often turn them off when they want a quieter desktop experience.

name: Disable Windows Media Player Telemetry
description: Turns off usage tracking and online metadata for Windows Media Player.

name: Display of the Last Signed-In Username
description: Windows can show the name of the last person who signed in on the sign-in screen. This setting decides whether that username is shown or hidden.

name: Start Personalized Site Recommendations
description: Windows 11 Start can surface personalized website suggestions. This device policy hides those recommendations for everyone on the machine.

name: Start Personalized Site Recommendations (Current User)
description: Windows 11 Start can surface personalized website suggestions. This user policy hides those recommendations just for the current account.

name: Start Menu Recommended Section
description: Windows 11 Start can show a Recommended section with suggested apps and files. This policy lets the device hide that section for everyone.

name: Start Menu Recommended Section (Current User)
description: Windows 11 Start can show a Recommended section with suggested apps and files. This user policy hides that section just for the current account.

name: Display of Username During Sign-In
description: After someone enters their credentials, Windows can keep showing the username or hide it. This setting decides whether the username stays visible during that sign-in flow.

name: Advanced Diagnostic Log Collection
description: Windows can collect extra diagnostic logs when advanced diagnostics are involved. This policy decides whether that additional log collection is limited.

name: Diagnostic Dump Collection
description: Windows can collect diagnostic dump data for troubleshooting. This policy decides whether that dump collection is limited.

name: Set Diagnostic Data to Minimum Supported Level
description: Windows can send different amounts of diagnostic data. This policy sets how much data Windows is allowed to collect and send.

name: Recommended Troubleshooting for Known Problems
description: Windows can automatically apply or suggest troubleshooting for known problems. This policy controls how much of that automation is allowed.

name: Turn Off Settings Sync by Default
description: Windows can sync settings like passwords, personalization, app settings, browser settings, and Start layout across devices. These policies control whether those categories are synced and whether users are allowed to turn syncing back on.

name: Microsoft Defender Sample Submission
description: Microsoft Defender can send file samples to Microsoft when cloud analysis needs them. This policy controls whether Defender prompts, sends safe samples, never sends, or sends all samples automatically.

name: Preserve Zone Information on Attachments
description: Windows normally tags downloaded files with where they came from, like the Internet or intranet. That information helps Windows decide when to warn or protect you. This policy controls whether that tagging happens.

name: Windows Security Enhanced Notifications
description: Windows Security can show non-critical notifications about device health and protection status. This policy hides those extra notifications so only critical ones remain.

name: Disable NTFS Encryption (EFS)
description: Windows can encrypt files on NTFS volumes by using EFS. This policy decides whether that encryption feature is allowed on NTFS volumes.

name: Delivery Optimization Download Mode
description: Delivery Optimization controls whether Windows uses other PCs to help download updates and Microsoft content. This policy sets how much peer-to-peer sharing Delivery Optimization is allowed to use.

name: Password Reveal Button
description: Windows can show an eye button next to password boxes so people can quickly check what they typed. This policy decides whether that button appears.

name: Picture Password Sign-In for Domain Users
description: Picture password lets someone sign in by tapping or drawing gestures on an image. This policy controls whether domain users are allowed to use that sign-in method.

name: Solicited Remote Assistance
description: Remote Assistance lets a user invite someone to help with the PC remotely. This policy decides whether that built-in help feature is allowed.

name: Disable System Mitigations
description: Imports the documented Exploit Protection XML baseline that disables the researched system-wide mitigation bundle.

name: Turn Off System Restore
description: System Restore lets Windows roll the system back to an earlier state after problems. This policy turns that recovery feature off.

name: Disable UAC (Full)
description: Disables User Account Control entirely. Requires a reboot and severely lowers system security.

name: Virtualization Based Security Policy Bundle
description: These Windows security features use virtualization to protect credentials and kernel integrity. This policy bundle turns those protections off.

name: Windows Defender Firewall Policy
description: Windows Defender Firewall protects the PC's network connections. The official policy can force the firewall on or off for managed profiles.

name: Windows Update Policy Control
description: These policies control whether Windows Update access is removed and whether automatic updates are prohibited.

name: Disable WPBT Execution
description: WPBT lets vendors and OEMs run a program from firmware during Windows startup. This tweak currently relies on a Session Manager registry value that is widely cited in community hardening material, but this research pass did not capture a primary Microsoft document that publishes that exact registry mapping.

name: Windows Update Driver Search Policy
description: When Windows needs a device driver, it can search Windows Update for one. These policies control whether that search is allowed and, if it is, when it happens.

name: Microsoft Defender MAPS Membership
description: Microsoft Defender can join Microsoft MAPS so the service can use cloud lookup and share more threat data with Microsoft.

name: Dynamic Lock
description: Dynamic Lock can automatically lock the PC when Windows decides the user is away, often based on Bluetooth signals.

name: Windows Sudo Mode Policy
description: Windows sudo lets elevated commands run from the command line. This policy decides whether sudo is allowed and, if it is, which interaction mode is the most permissive one users can use.

name: Hide Defender Exclusions From Local Admins
description: Defender can keep managed exclusions in effect but stop local admins from seeing them in the usual Defender admin surfaces.

name: Windows PowerShell Script Execution Policy
description: PowerShell can be configured to block scripts, allow only signed scripts, or allow all scripts. The official policy uses a Group Policy path to control that behavior.

name: Microsoft Defender Threat File Hash Logging
description: Defender can compute and log file hashes for some file-based detections, but the current 25H2 engine still exposes more than one registry surface for the setting.

name: Trusted Path for Credential Entry
description: This setting controls whether certain Windows credential prompts must happen on the Secure Desktop instead of inside the normal desktop session.

name: User Account Control Prompting Profile
description: These settings control whether Windows asks administrators before elevated actions and whether those prompts appear on the Secure Desktop.

name: Aero Shake Window Minimizing Gesture
description: Aero Shake is the gesture where you grab a window and shake it to minimize or restore other windows. This policy decides whether that gesture works for the current user.

name: Automatic Restart on System Failure
description: Windows can automatically restart the PC after a blue screen. Turning that off gives you time to see the crash screen and stop code before the machine reboots.

name: Display Blue Screen Parameters
description: This tweak tries to show extra technical parameters on a blue screen. That can help advanced debugging, but most users will not benefit from the extra numbers.

name: Automatic App Archiving
description: Windows can archive infrequently used apps to save space while keeping them restorable later. This policy decides whether that automatic archiving is allowed on the device.

name: Automatic Maintenance
description: Automatic Maintenance runs maintenance work like updates, scans, and housekeeping when Windows thinks the PC is idle. People disable it when they want tighter control over when maintenance runs.

name: Background Group Policy Refresh
description: Windows normally refreshes Group Policy in the background while the system is being used. This policy lets the device wait until logoff before applying those updates.

name: Clipboard History and Cross-Device Clipboard Sync
description: Windows can keep a history of copied items and can sync clipboard data across devices. These two policy values decide whether those features are allowed.

name: RDP Clipboard Redirection
description: Remote Desktop can let text and files move between your local clipboard and the remote machine. This policy controls whether that copy and paste bridge is allowed.

name: Fullscreen Optimizations
description: Fullscreen Optimizations is a Windows feature that tries to blend fullscreen-style game performance with some modern desktop and presentation behavior. People usually turn it off only when a specific game behaves badly with it.

name: Windows Game Recording and Broadcasting
description: Windows includes built-in game recording and broadcasting features. This policy decides whether those features are allowed on the device.

name: Wallpaper JPEG Import Quality
description: Windows can reduce the quality of JPEG images when you set them as wallpaper. People change this when they want the wallpaper to stay as sharp as possible.

name: Restart Apps After Sign-In
description: Windows can automatically save certain restartable apps and reopen them after you sign back in. People turn it off when they want a cleaner sign-in and do not want apps reopening on their own.

name: Telemetry and Maintenance Scheduled Tasks Bundle
description: This tweak turns off several Windows scheduled tasks related to compatibility, telemetry, cleanup, feedback, and error-reporting areas.

name: Search Highlights
description: Search Highlights are the dynamic bits Windows shows in the search area, such as seasonal or suggested content. This policy decides whether those highlights are allowed.

name: Remote Windows Search Queries
description: Windows Search can let other computers query this PC's search index over the network. This policy decides whether that remote index use is allowed.

name: Web Results in Windows Search
description: Windows Search can send queries to the web and show web results in the search experience. This policy decides whether that web-connected behavior is allowed.

name: Disable Service Splitting
description: Prevents services from being split into separate svchost processes.

name: Shortcut Arrow Overlay
description: Windows normally shows a small arrow on shortcut icons. This setting swaps that overlay resource so the arrow is no longer shown.

name: Startup Program Delay
description: Windows can stagger startup apps instead of launching them all immediately. People disable the delay when they want those apps to start sooner after sign-in, but that can also make startup load spike harder.

name: Storage Sense Automatic Cleanup
description: Storage Sense is Windows' automatic cleanup feature for temporary and unneeded files. This policy decides whether the feature is allowed at all on the device.

name: Storage Sense Temporary Files Cleanup
description: Storage Sense can automatically clean temporary files when Windows decides it is helpful. This policy controls that specific part of the cleanup behavior.

name: Store in Open With
description: When Windows cannot find an app for a file type, it can offer a Store-based option in the Open With dialog. This policy decides whether that Store option is available.

name: DWM: Disable Multiplane Overlay (MPO)
description: Disables MPO to avoid flicker or driver issues on some systems.

name: DWM Overlay Minimum FPS Check
description: Windows can use hardware overlays for some content, and one of the checks looks at how fast the surface is animating. This setting turns that minimum-FPS check off.

name: Game Mode
description: Game Mode is Windows' built-in gaming feature that tries to reduce interruptions and prioritize the current game. Most users either leave it on or benchmark it for a specific game.

name: Hardware-Accelerated GPU Scheduling
description: HAGS is a Windows graphics feature that lets the GPU take a more direct role in scheduling its work. It can help on some systems, but it can also make no noticeable difference or cause issues on others.

name: Indexing of Encrypted Files
description: Windows Search can be told to index encrypted files so their contents are searchable. That can make searching easier, but it also means Windows needs to process decrypted content during indexing.

name: Executive Additional Worker Threads
description: These values appear to control extra executive worker threads for internal critical and delayed work queues. They are low-level kernel-adjacent knobs and are being tracked as research only.

name: Graphics: Disable Overlay Planes
description: Disables overlay planes to reduce composition issues in some configurations.

name: Graphics: Page Fault Debug Mode
description: Restores the PageFaultDebugMode value to the documented default used by this tweak.

name: Graphics TDR DDI Delay
description: Windows gives graphics-driver threads a limited amount of time to leave the driver during TDR recovery. This setting controls that delay.

name: Graphics TDR Delay
description: Windows uses TDR to detect when the GPU takes too long to respond. This setting controls the main timeout threshold before recovery starts.

name: Graphics TDR Level
description: Windows can react to GPU timeouts in different ways, such as disabling detection or recovering on timeout. This setting controls that recovery mode.

name: Graphics TDR Limit Count
description: Windows keeps track of how many GPU hangs occur within the TDR time window. This setting controls that count threshold.

name: Graphics TDR Limit Time
description: Windows measures GPU hang events within a time window when deciding how to respond to repeated timeouts. This setting controls that time window.

name: Kernel: Adjust DPC Threshold
description: Sets the DPC threshold adjustment value to the documented default.

name: Kernel: Cache-Aware Scheduling
description: Restores Windows' documented cache-aware scheduling default so the scheduler stays aligned with normal CPU cache topology behavior.

name: Kernel: Default Dynamic Hetero CPU Policy
description: Returns Windows' hybrid CPU scheduling policy to the documented default used for heterogeneous core systems.

name: Kernel: Disable Low QoS Timer Resolution
description: Disables low QoS timer resolution using the documented default value.

name: Kernel: DPC Queue Depth
description: Sets the maximum DPC queue depth to the documented default.

name: Kernel: DPC Watchdog Period
description: Sets the DPC watchdog timeout to the documented default (milliseconds).

name: Kernel: Ideal DPC Rate
description: Sets the target DPC rate per second to the documented default.

name: Kernel: Minimum DPC Rate
description: Sets the minimum DPC rate threshold to the documented default.

name: Kernel: Serialize Timer Expiration
description: Enables timer serialization using the documented default value.

name: Threaded DPCs
description: Threaded DPCs let some kernel deferred work run in a way that can reduce system latency compared with ordinary DPCs. Most normal systems should leave this enabled.

name: Disable Exception Chain Validation
description: DisableExceptionChainValidation is a low-level Session Manager Kernel registry value tied to exception-chain policy handling during early boot.

name: Clear Page File at Shutdown
description: Windows can wipe the page file when the PC shuts down. This can reduce leftover data on disk, but it also makes shutdown take longer.

name: Disable Paging Executive
description: This setting was used for older tracing and diagnosis scenarios to keep some kernel-mode code and drivers in RAM instead of letting Windows page them out to disk. Microsoft says Windows 8 and newer systems do not need this change.

name: Large System Cache
description: Windows historically had a switch between favoring normal applications and favoring a larger system cache. Most normal users should leave this alone on modern systems.

name: Nonpaged Pool Size
description: Nonpaged pool is kernel memory that must always stay resident in RAM. This is a low-level legacy tuning area that normal users should not adjust manually.

name: Paged Pool Size
description: Paged pool is kernel memory that Windows can page out when needed. This is a legacy low-level memory tuning area that most people should never touch manually.

name: Registry Size Limit / Registry Quota
description: Windows historically exposed a registry size limit tied to paged-pool memory. Modern systems normally manage this automatically, so the safest reset is to return the published control to automatic sizing.

name: NTFS 8.3 Short Name Creation
description: NTFS can create old-style short file names for compatibility. Disabling them can reduce some filesystem overhead, but some legacy software still expects those short names to exist.

name: NTFS Last Access Time Updates
description: Windows can update a file or directory's last-access timestamp when it is accessed. Disabling these updates can reduce some disk overhead, but software that depends on last-access data can lose that signal.

name: Win32 Long Paths
description: Windows normally keeps many apps limited to shorter file paths. This setting allows long paths for apps that are built to support them.

name: NTFS Memory Usage
description: NTFS has an internal memory-usage tuning that affects its cache behavior. Most people should leave it at the default unless they have a proven file-server style workload.

name: NTFS MFT Zone Reservation
description: NTFS reserves some space for the master file table so it can grow with less fragmentation. This setting controls how large that reserved area is.

name: Foreground Scheduling Priority / Win32PrioritySeparation
description: This setting changes how Windows gives extra CPU time to the foreground application compared with background work. It is a low-level scheduler setting, not a normal everyday tweak.

name: Reliability Event Timestamping
description: Windows can timestamp reliability events on a cadence. This setting controls whether that timestamping behavior runs for the machine.

name: Bluetooth Audio Gateway Service
description: This service supports Bluetooth hands-free audio gateway features. Disabling it removes that capability.

name: Bluetooth Support Service
description: This is the main Windows Bluetooth support service. It helps Windows discover, pair, and work with Bluetooth devices.

name: Bluetooth User Service
description: This per-user Bluetooth service supports Bluetooth features tied to each signed-in user session. Disabling it removes those per-user Bluetooth service behaviors.

name: Connected User Experiences and Telemetry Service
description: This service handles Windows telemetry and connected-user-experience data collection. Disabling it reduces diagnostic and usage reporting, but some connected-experience features can lose functionality.

name: Print Device Configuration Service
description: This service manages installation details for IPP and UP printers. Disabling it can stop that printer-installation support.

name: Print Notification Service
description: This service opens custom printer dialogs and handles printer notifications. Disabling it removes those printer notifications and related extension dialogs.

name: Print Scan Broker Service
description: This service supports secure privileged operations needed by the lower-privilege print spooler components. Disabling it removes that support path.

name: Print Spooler Service
description: Print Spooler handles print jobs and manages interaction with printers. Disabling it removes Windows printing support on the device.

name: Print Workflow User Service
description: This per-user service supports Print Workflow applications. Disabling it can stop those print workflow features and may prevent some printing scenarios from working correctly.

name: SysMain Service
description: SysMain is Microsoft's documented background service for usage-pattern and preloading behavior. The record is deprecated because Microsoft guidance says not to disable it.

name: WAP Push Message Routing Service
description: This service routes Wireless Application Protocol push messages and helps synchronize some device-management sessions.

name: Windows Error Reporting Service
description: Windows Error Reporting collects crash and failure details so Windows can report problems and sometimes suggest or surface fixes.

name: Windows Search Service
description: Windows Search builds and maintains an index so file, email, and content searches can return indexed results without a full content crawl. Disabling it reduces indexing activity, but it also removes the indexed search experience.

name: Verbose Status Messages
description: Windows can either show simple loading screens or more detailed status text during startup, shutdown, sign-in, and sign-out. This policy decides whether the detailed messages are shown.

name: Service Shutdown Timeout
description: Windows waits a set amount of time for a service to stop cleanly during shutdown. Lowering that timeout reduces how long Windows waits, but it also gives services less time to flush state and clean up.

name: Default Account Picture for All Users
description: Windows normally lets each user choose their own account picture. This policy forces every user on the device to use the default account picture instead.

name: Acrylic Blur on the Logon Background
description: Windows can blur the logon background with an acrylic effect. This policy decides whether that blur is turned off so the background stays clear.

name: Common Control and Window Animations
description: Windows can animate common controls and some window transitions. This policy decides whether those animations are turned off for the current user.

name: First Sign-In Animation
description: Windows can show a first sign-in animation and, for Microsoft-account users, an opt-in prompt for services the first time someone signs in. This policy decides whether that first-run experience is shown.

name: Lock Screen
description: Windows normally shows a lock screen before the sign-in screen. This policy decides whether that lock screen appears.

name: Lock Screen Camera Access
description: Windows can allow a camera to be used directly from the lock screen. This policy decides whether that lock-screen camera access can be enabled.

name: Changing the Lock Screen and Logon Image
description: Windows normally lets users change the lock-screen and logon background image. This policy decides whether users are allowed to change those images.

name: Lock Screen Background Motion
description: Some devices can show a subtle motion effect on the lock-screen background. This policy decides whether that motion is prevented.

name: Lock Screen Slideshow
description: Windows can run a slideshow on the lock screen instead of always showing a single image. This policy decides whether users can use that slideshow feature.

name: Windows Spotlight on Action Center
description: Windows can show Spotlight-driven suggestions or prompts in Action Center style notification surfaces. This policy decides whether that content is allowed for the current user.

name: Spotlight Collection on Desktop
description: Windows can offer a Spotlight collection option for desktop backgrounds. This policy decides whether that Spotlight wallpaper option is allowed for the current user.

name: Windows Spotlight Features
description: Windows Spotlight powers various suggestions, tips, and promotional surfaces in Windows. This policy decides whether those Spotlight features are allowed for the current user.

name: Windows Spotlight on Settings
description: The Settings app can show Spotlight-based suggestions and highlights. This policy decides whether those Spotlight elements are allowed for the current user.

name: Third-Party Suggestions in Windows Spotlight
description: Windows Spotlight can include suggestions that point to third-party content or apps. This policy decides whether those suggestions are allowed for the current user.

name: Windows Spotlight Welcome Experience
description: Windows can show a Spotlight-based welcome or introductory experience after updates or sign-in. This policy decides whether that welcome experience is allowed for the current user.

name: Windows Connect Now Wizards
description: Windows Connect Now is an older wizard-based way to help set up some wireless routers and wireless devices. This policy decides whether those wizards are available.

name: Widgets Feature
description: Windows Widgets can show a board with news, weather, and other feed content. This policy decides whether the Widgets feature is allowed on the device at all.

name: Window Animations
description: Windows can animate windows when they open, close, minimize, and restore. This policy decides whether those window animations are allowed.

name: Control Panel Default View
description: Control Panel can open in either category view or the classic icons view. This policy chooses which one opens by default for the user.

name: Language Bar Visibility
description: The language bar shows keyboard or input-language controls. This tweak hides that UI for the current user.

name: Start Menu Most Used List
description: Windows can show a Most used list in Start to highlight apps you open often. This policy can force that list to be shown, hidden, or left under user control.

name: People Bar on the Taskbar
description: Windows used to offer a People Bar icon on the taskbar for quick contact access. This policy decides whether that feature is shown for the current user.

name: Classic Context Menu on Windows 11
description: Windows 11 normally shows the newer compact context menu. This tweak restores the older, fuller context menu style.
